CWE-20.name: Improper Input Validation
CWE-20.question: Does this function use input from outside, such as a quantity, index, type, structure or format, without checking it fully?

any: a length, count, index, offset or size from input drives allocation, loops, indexing or copying
parsed data such as JSON, XML or a binary record is used without checking its type, required fields, consistency or syntax
floating-point input or output is used without checking that it is finite
a validation framework or schema is present but bypassed or applied only to some fields
typescript: a request body, DTO or JSON.parse result is used under its declared interface or class type with no runtime check, as the type is erased when the code runs
a NestJS DTO carries class-validator decorators but no ValidationPipe applies to the route, so the decorators never execute

any: the function receives no external input, only values already validated or produced internally
all input is checked against explicit limits, types and formats before use on every path
typescript: the input goes through a zod, valibot, io-ts or ajv schema and only the parsed result is used
a ValidationPipe, global or on the route, validates a DTO whose class-validator decorators cover every field the function uses

CWE-74.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')

external values are passed solely through parameterised APIs, argument arrays or auto-escaping templates

CWE-75.name: Failure to Sanitize Special Elements into a Different Plane (Special Element Injection)
CWE-75.question: Does this function place input into a context where some characters have control meaning, such as delimiters, quotes, escape characters or equivalents, without neutralising them?

any: input is embedded in a delimited format, protocol line or control channel where separators or escape characters change meaning
a filter removes some special characters but encodings or alternative forms of the same characters may remain
user data is written into a stream that a downstream component parses for commands or fields
the data is encoded or escaped for the destination format, or carried in a separate field from control information
only constants or internal values reach the destination

CWE-76.name: Improper Neutralization of Equivalent Special Elements
CWE-76.question: Does this function filter or escape some special characters but miss other forms that mean the same thing, such as encoded, alternate or Unicode variants?

any: a sanitiser strips or escapes a specific character or sequence, such as ../ or <script>, while equivalent forms such as ..\, %2e%2e or upper-case tags remain

the data does not reach an interpreter or parser

input is quoted with a correct, context-specific escaping function before inclusion

CWE-1286.name: Improper Validation of Syntactic Correctness of Input
CWE-1286.question: Does this function accept structured input without checking it is well formed before using it?

any: a message, file or string expected to follow a grammar, such as JSON, XML, a date or an address, is split or indexed by hand without checking its structure
the result of parsing is used even when the parser reported an error or returned partial data
fields are extracted by fixed positions or separators and used without checking the expected count
input is parsed with a strict parser and any parse error stops processing
the function checks field counts and formats, and rejects malformed input, before using values

distinguish_from.CWE-112: the input is XML and is not checked against a schema
distinguish_from.CWE-1287: the input parses but its value has the wrong type

CWE-1287.name: Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input
CWE-1287.question: Does this function use an input value without checking that it is of the expected type, such as a number, string, list or object?

any: a field from parsed JSON, query parameters or a message is used as a number, string or array without checking its type
javascript: a request field is used with string methods, arithmetic or as an object key when it could be an array or object, for example from qs parsing
typescript: a request field declared string or number in a DTO or interface is used as that type with no typeof check, though at run time it may be an array or object
a value typed any or unknown is cast with as string, as number or as T and then used
python: a value from json.loads or request data is used assuming str or int without isinstance or conversion with error handling
c: a tagged message or union member is read without checking the type tag
cpp: a JSON value (for example nlohmann::json) is read with get<T>(), operator[] or implicit conversion without is_number(), is_string() or contains() checks
a std::variant is read with std::get, or a union member is read, without checking holds_alternative or index()

any: the value's type is checked, or it is converted with failure handling, before use
a strict schema or typed deserialiser has already enforced the type in this function
typescript: a schema parse or a typeof, Array.isArray or instanceof type guard confirms the type before the value is used
cpp: std::holds_alternative or the JSON type predicates are tested, or a typed from_json runs inside a try that handles type errors
rust: the value comes from a typed deserialiser such as serde into a concrete struct

distinguish_from.CWE-1286: the input is not even syntactically well formed
distinguish_from.CWE-843: memory is accessed as a different type from the one it holds

CWE-1288.name: Improper Validation of Consistency within Input
CWE-1288.question: Does this function use several related input fields without checking they agree with each other, such as a length field against the data actually supplied?

any: a declared length, count or checksum in a header is trusted without comparing it with the size of the payload received
start and end values, minimum and maximum, or a total and its parts are used without checking their relationship
duplicate or conflicting keys in input, such as two values for the same parameter, are accepted without rule
related fields are cross-checked, for example start <= end and declared length equals received length, and mismatches are rejected
only one field is used and the others are ignored

distinguish_from.CWE-1284: a single quantity is unchecked, with no relationship between fields involved
distinguish_from.CWE-130: a length field inconsistent with the data leads to a memory access

CWE-1289.name: Improper Validation of Unsafe Equivalence in Input
CWE-1289.question: Does this function check an identifier or reference for a forbidden value without first normalising it, so an equivalent spelling passes?

any: a deny check compares a name, path, host or tag case-sensitively when the consumer treats it case-insensitively
input is checked before URL decoding, Unicode normalisation or path resolution that happens later
a blocked value is compared literally while alternate forms such as trailing dots, extra slashes or IP address encodings are not considered
the value is canonicalised, for example decoded, normalised, lower-cased or resolved, before the check, and the canonical form is what gets used
the check is an exact allow list match on the canonical form
the value is not used as a resource identifier or security reference

distinguish_from.CWE-76: the escaping or neutralisation handles one special element but not its equivalents
distinguish_from.CWE-186: the check is a regex that is too narrow to catch variants

CWE-1336.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
CWE-1336.question: Does this function feed untrusted input to a template engine as template source, or render it in a way the engine will evaluate?

any: a template string is built by concatenating or formatting input and then compiled or rendered
input is passed as the template body rather than as a context variable
python: Template(input), render_template_string, Environment.from_string or format_map on a string that includes input
javascript: ejs.render, pug.compile, Handlebars.compile, nunjucks.renderString or lodash _.template called on a string containing input

any: the template source is a fixed file or constant and input is supplied only as data in the render context
a sandboxed or logic-less engine is used and the input is still only data

distinguish_from.CWE-95: input reaches eval or Function directly without a template engine

CWE-1427.name: Improper Neutralization of Input Used for LLM Prompting
CWE-1427.question: Does this function place untrusted text into a prompt for a language model without keeping it separate from the developer's instructions?

any: user input, retrieved documents or web content is concatenated or interpolated into the system prompt or instruction text
untrusted text is merged into the same message as instructions with no role separation or delimiting
model output driven by untrusted content is used to choose tools, commands or actions without checks
untrusted content is sent only as a separate user-role message, with fixed instructions in the system role
the prompt is built entirely from constants or trusted configuration
the function does not call or prepare input for a language model
